facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with an enlarging purpuric patch on his left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
initially present for 2 weeks
the lesion first developed in March 2014 and was fairly stable until June 2014
rapid growth and extension followed by central ulceration and bleeding
a 30 × 25-cm centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
involving: Left anterior scalp with extension posteriorly on left parietal scalp
No evidence of lymphadenopathy in preauricular, cervical, occipital, submandibular or supraclavicular areas
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
No evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases
Staging: T2N0M0
